correctness.rationale: The repaired theorem retains the frozen Finding. In frozen RESULT.md lines 80–82 the relative error O(exp(-at)) is false for a>1: at lambda=a the normalized error is asymptotic to -exp(-t), from the numerator of h. The repair keeps that numerator exactly and factors the denominator as 1-delta, delta=(1+lambda-2 lambda exp(-t))exp(-lambda t)/2. On the whole compact rate interval, delta=O(exp(-at)) and its lambda derivative is O(t exp(-at)) at late times. Thus the relative error is O(exp(-min(a,1)t)), and the log derivative is 1/lambda+1/(1+lambda)-t+O(t exp(-at)), strictly negative uniformly for large t. The three relevant forward equations have no incoming paths from other states; integrating them gives the stated masses. Pair weighting gives W1=2A+D and W2=2B, so the ratio B/W1 gives the covariance comparison under the W1-weighted law. It has lambda derivative t+O(t^2) uniformly at early times. The weighted law remains nondegenerate, so the two-draw covariance identity gives strict signs even for discrete or singular mixtures. Both masses are positive for finite t>0, and continuity yields existence, not uniqueness, of an equality. Complete corrected RESULT.md and VERIFICATION.md are in repairs/5. Bounded independent replay: python3 /workspace/check_frozen_mathematics.py 5 (NumPy/SciPy matrix exponential and Decimal). Three discrete laws give opposite signs at t=0.03 and 12; at lambda=2 the old relative error multiplied by exp(t) tends numerically to -1. The computations do not establish the universal assertions; the repaired analytic proof does. The verification notes distinguish the 126 transient comparisons from other assertions.

value.rationale: The three-person group is the smallest with both relevant infectious counts and remaining susceptibility. Strict reversal for all nondegenerate compact positive mixtures is a structural distinction between pooled conditional association and the underlying linear hazard, not just an example or failure of a short-time approximation. It sharpens how a calibration time can affect inference in a precisely defined statistical model. Late at-risk pairs may be very rare; the finding is not a claim about empirical estimability or actual epidemics.
